findings.title: New abstract interface method breaks third-party CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `int order()` is added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract method with no default. Any existing external implementation of `CryptoProvider` will fail to compile, and at runtime an `AbstractMethodError` is thrown when `detectProvider` calls `order()` during sorting. Making it a `default` method (for example returning 0) would keep backward compatibility.

findings.title: Ties between equal-order providers resolved silently and nondeterministically
findings.body: Default, Elytron and FIPS providers all return 200. Previously, having more than one on the classpath was a hard error. Now the first one in ServiceLoader (classpath) order wins and the others are only mentioned in a debug log. A misconfigured deployment, for example FIPS and the default provider both present, could quietly run with the non-FIPS provider. Consider still failing when the top two providers have the same order.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary keystore provider
findings.body: This method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (for example SUN or SunJSSE), not a BouncyCastle provider. Code that calls `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` or uses this provider for cipher or signature operations may get an unexpected provider or fail with `NoSuchAlgorithmException`.

findings.title: Indefinite length returns -1 and causes NegativeArraySizeException
findings.body: `readLength` returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80). `readInteger` then calls `read(-1)`, which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an `IOException`. In `readSequence` the loop is skipped and an empty list is returned. Malformed signatures therefore produce unchecked exceptions rather than a clean verification failure.
